description: Tab Brain - AI-Powered Chrome Extension for Smart Tab Grouping & Knowledge Capture

userStories.title: Project scaffold with Manifest V3
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Chrome extension project structure so all subsequent stories have a foundation to build on.
acceptanceCriteria: Create manifest.json with Manifest V3: permissions [tabs, tabGroups, sidePanel, storage, activeTab], service_worker, side_panel, options_page
Create empty service-worker.js that registers successfully
Create sidepanel.html with minimal HTML boilerplate, plus empty sidepanel.js and sidepanel.css
Create options.html with minimal HTML boilerplate, plus empty options.js and options.css
Create lib/ directory with empty placeholder files: ai.js, grouper.js, tracker.js, knowledge.js
Extension loads in chrome://extensions developer mode without errors
No JavaScript errors in service worker console
userStories.notes: Plain JavaScript, no TypeScript, no build tools. Keep it simple. Project files go in the repo root (manifest.json at root level).

userStories.title: Options page for API key configuration
userStories.description: As a user, I need to configure my Anthropic API key and endpoint so the extension can call Claude for tab grouping.
acceptanceCriteria: Options page has input fields: API Key (password type), API Endpoint URL (default: https://api.anthropic.com), Model (default: claude-sonnet-4-20250514)
Save button stores settings to chrome.storage.sync
On page load, existing settings are populated from chrome.storage.sync
Show success/error feedback after save
Basic validation: API key is required, endpoint must be a valid URL
Clean, minimal CSS styling
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: This is the first-run setup. Without an API key, grouping falls back to offline domain-based mode.

userStories.title: AI client module for Claude API
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a reusable AI client module so the grouper and other features can call Claude API.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/ai.js exports a sendMessage(systemPrompt, userMessage) function
Reads API key, endpoint, and model from chrome.storage.sync
Makes POST request to {endpoint}/v1/messages with correct headers (x-api-key, anthropic-version, content-type)
Returns parsed response content text
10-second timeout via AbortController; throws descriptive error on timeout
Throws descriptive error if API key is not configured
Throws descriptive error if response is not OK (includes status code)
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: Use fetch API. The endpoint default is https://api.anthropic.com. Model default is claude-sonnet-4-20250514. anthropic-version header should be 2023-06-01.

userStories.title: Tab metadata collection module
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a module to collect all open tab metadata so it can be sent to the AI for grouping.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/tabs.js exports a getAllTabs() function
Uses chrome.tabs.query({}) to get all tabs across all windows
Returns array of objects: {index (0-based position), tabId (Chrome tab ID), title, url, domain, favIconUrl, pinned, windowId}
Pinned tabs are included in the result but marked with pinned: true
Domain is extracted from URL (hostname only, e.g., 'github.com')
Handles edge cases: chrome:// URLs, empty titles, data: URLs
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: The 0-based index is a position index assigned by us (not chrome tab ID). This is what gets sent to the AI. We map back to tabId after AI response.

userStories.title: AI-powered tab grouping logic
userStories.description: As a user, I want the AI to analyze my tabs and create meaningful Chrome Tab Groups so my tabs are organized by topic.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/grouper.js exports a groupTabsWithAI(tabs) function
Constructs grouping prompt with tab list as JSON (index, title, url, pinned flag)
Prompt instructs AI to: group by semantic topic, return JSON with groups (name, color, tab indices), skip pinned tabs, max 8 groups, for <8 tabs use ceil(tabCount/2) groups
Sends prompt via lib/ai.js sendMessage()
Parses AI JSON response to extract group assignments
After AI response, re-queries chrome.tabs.query() to handle tabs that closed during the call
Applies groups via chrome.tabs.group() and chrome.tabGroups.update() with name and color
Skips tab indices whose tabs no longer exist; assigns new tabs opened during call to 'Misc' group
Returns summary object: {groups: [{name, color, tabCount}], totalGrouped, skipped}
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: Valid Chrome Tab Group colors: grey, blue, red, yellow, green, pink, purple, cyan, orange. AI prompt should specify these exact values. If AI returns invalid JSON, throw an error (fallback handled by caller).

userStories.title: Offline fallback grouping by domain
userStories.description: As a user, I want tabs grouped by domain when AI is unavailable so I still get some organization without an API key.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/grouper.js exports a groupTabsByDomain(tabs) function
Groups tabs by eTLD+1 domain (e.g., all github.com tabs together, all stackoverflow.com together)
Assigns colors from a predefined rotation (blue, green, cyan, orange, purple, pink, red, yellow)
Domains with only 1 tab go into a 'Misc' group (grey)
Skips pinned tabs
Applies groups via same chrome.tabs.group() + chrome.tabGroups.update() API
lib/grouper.js exports a main groupTabs() function that tries AI first, falls back to domain grouping on any error
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: The main groupTabs() function is the public API. It calls groupTabsWithAI() first, catches any error (no API key, timeout, parse failure), then calls groupTabsByDomain() as fallback.

userStories.title: Service worker event wiring
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the service worker to handle messages from the side panel and coordinate module interactions.
acceptanceCriteria: service-worker.js imports and uses modules from lib/
Handles chrome.runtime.onMessage for action 'groupNow': calls groupTabs() and returns result
Handles chrome.runtime.onMessage for action 'getTabStats': returns current tab count and group count
Sets chrome.sidePanel.setPanelBehavior({ openPanelOnActionClick: true }) on install
Handles errors gracefully and returns error messages to caller
No JavaScript errors in service worker console
userStories.notes: Use importScripts() or static import for ES modules (need type:module in manifest). Prefer ES modules if supported.

userStories.title: Side panel layout and Group Now button
userStories.description: As a user, I want a side panel with a 'Group Now' button so I can trigger AI tab grouping with one click.
acceptanceCriteria: sidepanel.html has a header 'Tab Brain' with current tab count
A prominent 'Group Now' button that sends 'groupNow' message to service worker
Loading spinner/state shown while grouping is in progress, button disabled during loading
On success: shows summary (number of groups created, total tabs grouped)
On error: shows error message with fallback suggestion
Clean, minimal CSS: dark sidebar theme, good contrast, readable typography
Responsive within side panel width constraints
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: Side panel is typically 300-400px wide. Design for this constraint. Use CSS custom properties for theming.

userStories.title: Side panel displays current tab groups
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my current tab groups in the side panel so I can understand how my tabs are organized.
acceptanceCriteria: Side panel shows a 'Current Groups' section listing all Chrome Tab Groups
Each group shows: color indicator (matching Chrome group color), group name, tab count
Groups are expandable/collapsible to show individual tab titles under each group
Clicking a tab title activates that tab (chrome.tabs.update with active:true and window.focus)
Ungrouped tabs shown under an 'Ungrouped' section
Group list refreshes after 'Group Now' completes
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: Use chrome.tabGroups.query() to get groups and chrome.tabs.query({groupId}) to get tabs in each group. Handle the case where user has no groups yet.

userStories.title: IndexedDB setup and tab activity tracker
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an IndexedDB-backed activity tracker so we can record tab usage for knowledge base and stale detection.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/knowledge.js creates/opens IndexedDB database 'TabBrainDB' with object store 'entries'
Schema per entry: {url, title, domain, favIconUrl, firstSeen, lastSeen, totalFocusTime, category, archived}
Indexes on: url (unique), domain, lastSeen, archived
Exports functions: saveEntry(entry), getEntry(url), updateEntry(url, updates), getAllEntries(), searchEntries(query), pruneOldEntries(maxAgeDays)
lib/tracker.js listens to chrome.tabs.onActivated to track focus events
On tab focus: upsert entry with updated lastSeen and accumulated totalFocusTime
Auto-prune entries older than 90 days on startup
Service worker imports and initializes tracker on install/activate
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: totalFocusTime tracks cumulative seconds the tab was focused. On onActivated, record timestamp; on next onActivated, calculate duration and add to previous tab's totalFocusTime. IndexedDB writes must be async and non-blocking.

userStories.title: Stale tab detection and close recommendations
userStories.description: As a user, I want the extension to recommend closing stale tabs so I can reduce clutter without losing information.
acceptanceCriteria: Stale tab detection: tabs not focused in 3+ days (based on tracker data in IndexedDB)
Side panel shows 'Stale Tabs' section with count of stale tabs
Each stale tab listed with title, domain, and days since last focused
Each stale tab has an individual 'Archive & Close' button
'Archive & Close All' button at the top of the stale section
Archive action: saves/updates entry in knowledge base with archived:true, then closes tab via chrome.tabs.remove()
Stale list refreshes after archiving
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: Compare tab's lastSeen in IndexedDB with Date.now(). If no IndexedDB entry exists for a tab, treat it as non-stale (we haven't tracked it long enough). Show empty state message when no stale tabs found.

userStories.title: Knowledge base search UI
userStories.description: As a user, I want to search my browsing history in the side panel so I can find pages I visited before without reopening tabs.
acceptanceCriteria: Side panel shows 'Knowledge Base' section with statistics: tabs tracked today, this week
Search input with placeholder 'Search knowledge...'
Full-text search across titles, URLs, and domains in IndexedDB
Search results show: title, domain, last seen date, total focus time, archived badge if applicable
Clicking a search result opens the URL in a new tab
Results limited to 20 items with most recent first
Empty state when no results match
No JavaScript errors in console
userStories.notes: Search implementation: iterate IndexedDB entries and filter by query substring match on title+url+domain. For v1 this is fine up to a few thousand entries. Debounce search input (300ms).
